content.value_statement: Apple menu and button choices can become inconsistent across platforms. This skill applies HIG guidance for menus, toolbars, buttons, and related controls.
actual_capabilities: Recommends menu, button, toolbar, and disclosure components for Apple interfaces.
Compares context menus, pull-down buttons, pop-up buttons, and action buttons.
Summarizes placement, grouping, labels, icons, roles, and visual hierarchy.
Highlights platform considerations for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, and visionOS.
Checks existing Apple design context before asking follow-up questions.
limitations: Does not generate production UI code by itself.
Does not replace testing with real Apple platform controls.
Focused on menus, buttons, toolbars, and disclosure controls, not every HIG component.
Reference content may need checking against current Apple documentation for recent changes.

use_cases.title: Plan Mac Command Menus
use_cases.description: Map common commands into menu bar, Help, Window, and app-specific menus.

use_cases.title: Choose Compact Controls
use_cases.description: Select between pop-up, pull-down, action, and standard buttons for constrained layouts.

use_cases.title: Review Cross-Platform Toolbars
use_cases.description: Check toolbar actions, grouping, overflow behavior, and platform differences before handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a Button Type
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend the best Apple HIG button or menu component for this action: [describe action]. Platforms: [platforms]. Explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Toolbar
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this toolbar plan against Apple HIG: [paste actions and layout]. Suggest grouping, overflow, and placement changes for [platforms].

prompt_templates.title: Design Menu Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a menu and toolbar strategy for a [app type] on macOS and iPadOS. Include command locations, shortcuts, and fallback access.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Cross-Platform Tradeoffs
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare menu, toolbar, pull-down, and context-menu options for [workflow]. Recommend platform-specific behavior for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, and visionOS.

output_examples.input: Need a control for selecting one sort order from many options.
output_examples.output: Use a pop-up button when space is limited and one selection is active. Add a clear label so users can predict the choices.

output_examples.input: Need secondary actions for a document card.
output_examples.output: Use a context menu for secondary actions, but keep important commands available elsewhere. Group actions by task and mark destructive items clearly.

output_examples.input: Need frequent editing commands on iPad and Mac.
output_examples.output: Place the most common commands in the toolbar, keep standard edit commands in expected menus, and define overflow behavior for narrow widths.

best_practices: Start with the user primary action, then choose the smallest control that keeps it discoverable.
Keep destructive commands visually distinct and require confirmation when the platform pattern supports it.
Check platform sections before reusing a menu or toolbar pattern across Apple devices.
anti_patterns: Hiding primary actions only inside context menus or pull-down buttons.
Creating custom button styles that mimic reserved system states.
Adding many toolbar items without grouping, overflow behavior, or customization.

faq.question: What does this skill help design?
faq.answer: It helps choose and structure Apple menus, buttons, toolbars, and disclosure controls.

faq.question: Which platforms does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers guidance for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, and visionOS when the references include platform notes.

faq.question: Can it choose between pop-up and pull-down buttons?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when to use selection controls, action lists, context menus, and standard buttons.

faq.question: Does it create application code?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance and recommendations, not implementation-ready source code.

faq.question: Can it review an existing toolbar plan?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the actions, layout, and target platforms so it can suggest grouping and overflow improvements.

faq.question: Does it replace Apple documentation?
faq.answer: No. It organizes local HIG reference material and should be checked against current Apple documentation for critical releases.
